limitations: Branch-only experiment; no merge to main, image registry push or formal release.
One frozen Grype database and the same pinned native Syft/Grype versions were used for all eight scans. Positive/negative Guava controls are retained.
Raw finding/advisory counts reflect vendor feed, package splitting and JVM identification differences. A lower count does not prove proportionally lower exploitable risk.
JVM inventory/matches are recorded separately. Neither source proves exhaustive JVM vulnerability coverage.
Certificate regression is offline historical-time PKIX validation with normal and restored-root controls, not live HTTPS/RDS/PolarDB certification.
The experiment does not change or satisfy the production Trivy gate. Workflow execution success alone does not indicate production readiness.

Initial preparation attempts stopped before image construction: whole-file hashing exceeded 2 GiB, then Skopeo rejected a combined tag/digest reference. The retained script uses bounded reads and digest-only Skopeo references.

conclusion.functional: All four native candidate runtime suites and all eight offline certificate regressions passed.
conclusion.security: HIGH entries decreased from 17 to 0, but total entries increased from 66 to 84 and unique CVEs from 41 to 44 in every pair. No overall CVE reduction was demonstrated.
conclusion.coverage: Workflow intentionally failed its repaired OpenTelemetry inventory assertion; Syft reports 1.62.0 despite embedded 1.67.0 metadata and exact official repaired bytes. This is not a fully accepted Java dependency scan.
conclusion.java: Candidate runs Red Hat Java 25.0.4.1+1; baseline runs Temurin 25.0.5+8-LTS. The candidate reports 80 JVM package findings representing 40 CVEs, whereas the baseline has no JVM matches in the Debian vendor feed; do not interpret that as exhaustive baseline JVM clearance.
conclusion.recommendation: Retain the branch for evaluation. Do not adopt the candidate based on these results: total CVEs did not decrease, its JVM patch version differs and Java SBOM identification needs resolution.
